title: Qualitative growth potential test for brackish _Vaucheria_ species
protocol: Take samples from the bare sediment scooping at least 50 ml of material from the upper layer (~1 cm) using the sample container.
Label the sample containers according to the sample location and replicate number.
Sample patches with clear Vaucheria presence as positive control in addition to bare sediment samples.
Prepare 2 tissue culture flasks and 1 Erlenmeyer per sample for incubation and negative control.
Take the samples from the freezer and let them thaw to room temperature.
Place the Erlenmeyer flask on a balance.
Sterilise the metal spatula in the Bunsen flame.
Bring approximately 50 grams of sediment into the Erlenmeyer flask using the sterilised spatula.
Add 2 ml of sterilised tap water to the Erlenmeyer flask and homogenize by stirring and gently shaking.
Place the tissue culture flask on a balance.
Bring approximately 20 grams of homogenized sample into the tissue culture flask using the spatula.
Add 20 ml of MDV medium to the tissue culture flask.
Gently shake the tissue culture flask so that the sediment is evenly spread across the growth surface.
Close the Erlenmeyer flask with cotton wool.
Sterilize the samples for 15 min at 121°C using the autoclave.
Place the tissue culture flask on a balance.
Sterilize the metal spatula in the Bunsen flame.
Bring approximately 20 grams of sterilized sample into the flask using the spatula.
Add 20 ml of MDV medium to the flask.
Gently shake so that the sediment is evenly spread across the flask wall.
Place the tissue culture flask in the climate room for incubation for at least 6 weeks.
Ensure the temperature and light conditions are set as described.
Gently shake the flasks once every couple of days to ensure nutrients are distributed well and gas exchange is facilitated.
Extend the incubation time with a few more weeks if no clear visible signs of filamentous algae are present.
Inspect the culture flasks for the development of green pigments on the sediment surface.
Document the presence of green pigments as an indication of good growth conditions for benthic algae.
Observe the flask more carefully if filaments are present, indicating a likely positive sample for _Vaucheria_.
Use a magnifying glass or microscope to confirm the presence of weakly developed filaments.
Further inspect the flasks using a magnifying glass or microscope to ensure the filaments are _Vaucheria_.
Identify _Vaucheria_ at the species level in well-developed samples if they are sexually mature.
Take pictures of the tissue culture flasks at the start and end of incubation.
